name: OPA2107 / OPA2107AP / OPA2107AU
tagline: Burr-Brown Difet JFET dual (4.5 MHz, 18 V/µs) rollers call warm and full; HiFiMAN paired it with OPA627 in HM-801/901.

lineage.note: PDS-863, ©1989 (original January 1989); editions B 1993-10, E 1998-04. Macromodel Rev A 10/17/90; OPA2107E model 3/21/92.
Bought Burr-Brown in 2000. Reissued as SBOS161 (rev A, July 2003); PSpice model SBOM045. No second source.

part_numbers.note: DIP-8, the rolling version; c't Lab AD16-8 specifies it. Obsolete per DigiKey.
SO-8; -2K5 = 2,500-piece tape and reel. Reportedly obsolete. Model CMRR 92 dB.
TO-99 inferred from M suffix; 1996 EWB libraries only. Model Aol 63,000, CMRR 94 dB.
Likely TO-99 top grade. Models: Aol 100,000, CMRR 100 dB, Vos 50–100 µV, half bias.
TO-99, presumably military-temperature grade; only in 1996 EWB libraries.

key_specs.value: 8 nV/√Hz (at 10 kHz; 1 kHz value not seen)
±4.5 V to ±18 V (9 V to 36 V)
<2.5 mA per amp (a listing says 4.5 mA/ch)
1 mV max (early edition 500 µV); drift 10 µV/°C max
P-channel JFET pair, Difet dielectric isolation

reputation.summary: A cult favourite of the Head-Fi rolling era. Forums, Japanese blogs and Zigsow call it warm, full and tube-like, between OPA2604 and OPA627. Soomal groups it in a warm, spacious 'DiFET' sound but says OPA627/637 resolve treble better. HiFiMAN used it in several players; c't Lab calls it 'weit besser' than a TL072. No independent measurements.
typical_uses: DAC low-pass filter: HiFiMAN HM-901 (2013), with OPA627
DAP analogue stage: HiFiMAN HM-801 (2009), with OPA627
Portable amp stage: HiFiMAN HM-602 (2010), HM-601LE (2014)
DIP-8 op-amp rolling in DACs and preamps
Precision ADC/DAC input amp: c't Lab AD16-8, DA12-8
caveats: Obsolete at TI (OPA2107AP per DigiKey); supply is NOS or pulled stock.
Needs a fairly high supply: Tangent measured 10.6 V minimum (OPA627: 6.8/9.8 V); Digi-Key price then $12.25.
Modest output current (about 40 mA per models); buffer it for low-impedance headphones.
Praise is mostly forum impression; Soomal's 'DiFET' group includes non-Difet OPA2134, and its HM-901 reviewers hadn't heard it elsewhere.
NOS remark risk is a general concern for obsolete audio op-amps; no OPA2107-specific report.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA2107-specific fake reports. Stock is NOS, pulled or broker parts, even die. Check logo era (BB vs TI) against date code and marking. Genuine parts show pA bias, ~18 V/µs and ~4.5 MHz; remarked bipolar parts show nA bias.
alternatives: Two OPA627 on a dual adapter

revision_history.changes: Initial release; date inferred from the SBOS161A header and ©1989 notice. Letter and copy not seen.
PDS-863B, printed October 1993, ©1989. Change content unknown.
PDS-863E, printed April 1998; last Burr-Brown edition seen. Change content unknown; C and D not seen.
Headline Vos relaxed from 500 µV max (rtellason copy) to 1 mV max by PDS-863E; which edition changed it is unknown.
TI reissue, 'January 1989 - revised July 2003': 1 mV max Vos, 10 µV/°C, 10 pA, 8 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz. Changes unknown.

revision_chains.note: Original letter (unlettered or A) unseen; 1989 databook or 1990 Supplement 33b may hold it.
SBOS161A appears final. The focus.ti.com seed is a pattern guess; burr-brown.com-era URL not found.

open_questions: Which mirror holds which edition (PDS-863B, PDS-863E, SBOS161A), and what changed between editions?
Find the PDS-863 original or PDS-863A, PDS-863C, PDS-863D and unlettered SBOS161; check the 1989 databook and 1990 Supplement 33b.
TI obsolescence date, PCN/EOL number and last-time-buy? Are AU and AU-2K5 obsolete? Any TI-era fab transfer?
Resolve Iq: under 2.5 mA per amplifier (datasheet) vs 4.5 mA 'per channel' (parametric listing).
Datasheet 1 kHz noise, i_n, THD+N, Aol/CMRR? When were TO-99 grades dropped? Did the HM-601 (non-LE) use it?
